t.1.204.2: Having taken all the treasures of the Devas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Nāgas, kings and Rākṣasas, the two attained supreme satisfaction.
t.1.204.1: Nārada said: Having conquered the earth, the two Daityas, now without rivals and free from anxiety, brought the three worlds to a state of calm and considered their purpose fulfilled.
t.1.204.3: When there was no one here at all who could oppose those two, they became free of exertion and took their pleasure like two immortals.
t.1.204.4: With women, garlands and perfumes, with abundant foods both chewed and soft, and with various delightful drinks, the two attained the highest pleasure.
t.1.204.5: In the women's quarters, in forest gardens, and in groves upon the mountains, and in whatever places they desired, the two took their pleasure like two immortals.
t.1.204.6: Then one day the two went off to amuse themselves on a level stretch of rock on the ridge of the Vindhya, among śāla trees whose crowns were in bloom.
t.1.204.7: When all heavenly objects of desire had been brought together there, the two of them, delighted, sat down on excellent seats together with the women.
t.1.204.8: Then women waited upon the two of them with instrumental music and dances, and they approached them with songs joined with praises for the sake of pleasing them.
t.1.204.9: Then Tilottamā, gathering flowers there in the forest, put on a captivating attire, clad in a single red garment.
t.1.204.10: Gathering the karṇikāra flowers that grew along the riverbanks, she slowly went to the place where the two great Asuras were.
t.1.204.11: But those two, having drunk the choicest drink, their eyes red at the corners with intoxication, became agitated the moment they saw her, the fair-hipped one.
t.1.204.12: The two of them sprang up, left their seats, and went to where she stood; both were maddened with desire, and both began to woo her.
t.1.204.13: Sunda seized that fair-browed woman by her right hand with his hand, and Upasunda too seized Tilottamā by her left hand.
t.1.204.14: Those two were intoxicated by the granting of the boon, by their innate strength, by the twin intoxications of wealth and jewels, and by the intoxication of drinking wine.
t.1.204.15: Intoxicated by all these intoxications and frowning at one another, the two, overcome by frenzy and desire, then spoke to each other.
t.1.204.16: Sunda said, “She is my wife, and therefore your elder to be revered!” Upasunda said, “She is my wife, and therefore your daughter-in-law!”
t.1.204.18: The two of them, bewildered by desire for her, seized their terrible maces and struck each other down, each crying, "I first! I first!"
t.1.204.17: "She is not yours, she is mine!" Thus, there, wrath took hold of the two of them, and for her sake both of them seized their terrible maces.
t.1.204.19: Struck down by their maces, those two fearsome ones fell upon the surface of the earth, their limbs smeared with blood, like two suns fallen from the sky.
t.1.204.20: Then those women fled, and the whole host of Daityas, trembling with despair and fear, went down to Pātāla.
t.1.204.21: Then the Grandfather, pure of soul, came there together with the gods and the great seers, intending to honor Tilottamā.
t.1.204.22: Offered a boon by Brahmā, she chose only his affection; then the Grandfather, pleased, spoke to her.
t.1.204.24: Having thus granted her the boon, the Lord, the Grandfather of all the worlds, entrusted the three worlds to Indra and went to the world of Brahmā.
t.1.204.23: You shall roam the worlds traversed by Āditya, O lovely lady, and because of your splendor no one will be able to look upon you clearly.
t.1.204.25: Thus those two, who had always been united and of one resolve in all matters, became enraged over Tilottamā and struck each other down.
t.1.204.26: Therefore, out of affection, I say to all of you, best of the Bharatas: act in such a way that no division may arise among all of you here on account of Draupadī. Good fortune be with you, if you wish to do what is dear to me.
t.1.204.27: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the great seer Nārada, O king, those great-souled ones, coming together with one another, made a compact in the very presence of that divine seer Nārada of boundless might.
t.1.204.29: When that agreement had been made by the Pāṇḍavas, who walked the path of dharma, the great sage Nārada, well pleased, departed for the place he desired.
t.1.204.28: Whoever among us should see one of the others sitting with Draupadī, he among us shall dwell in the forest for twelve years as a celibate.
t.1.204.30: Thus, urged on by Nārada, they had earlier made a compact, and then, O Bhārata, none of them was divided from one another.
